claim: Dist2ill trains an LLM to produce multiple diverse reasoning paths within a single inference pass, paired with a lightweight parametric module that approximates the empirical confidence score normally derived from full sampling-based marginalization.
stance_target: cheap single-pass approximations can recover the sampling-based uncertainty signal
scope_conditions: discriminative and (as of v3, Feb 2026) generative reasoning tasks; not specified as code generation
quoted_support: To enable accurate uncertainty estimation in a single forward pass, we propose a novel distributional distillation framework (Dist2ill) that trains an LLM to produce multiple diverse reasoning paths within one inference pass, while using a lightweight parametric module to approximate empirical confidence scores derived from the sampling distribution.

claim: Bayesian treatments (marginalizing over a weight posterior or over the space of reasoning traces) provide effective uncertainty estimates but incur substantial computational overhead due to repeated sampling at test time.
stance_target: sampling-based confidence is accurate but expensive
quoted_support: Bayesian treatments, such as marginalizing over a reliable weight posterior or over the space of reasoning traces, provide an effective remedy, but incur substantial computational overhead due to repeated sampling at test time.

claim: Dist2ill preserves reasoning diversity while achieving state-of-the-art uncertainty estimation, substantially improving Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL), while remaining computationally efficient.
stance_target: single-pass distillation methods can match or beat sampling-based calibration quality at much lower cost
scope_conditions: benchmarks tested in the paper; exact datasets not specified in abstract
quoted_support: Extensive experiments demonstrate that Dist2ill preserves reasoning diversity and achieves state-of-the-art uncertainty estimation, substantially improving Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL), while remaining computationally efficient.

claim: Dist2ill was extended from a discriminative-reasoning-only method (v1/v2, May 2025) to a unified framework supporting both discriminative and generative reasoning (v3, Feb 2026), indicating the single-pass distillation approach generalizes across task formats over an ~9-month development period.
stance_target: maturity/generality of single-pass distillation UQ methods
quoted_support: 05/2025 (v1&v2): Introduced Dist2ill (previously named EUD) for efficient uncertainty estimation, focusing on discriminative reasoning tasks. 02/2026 (v3): Extended Dist2ill to a unified framework supporting both discriminative and generative reasoning
